beats.summary: Jim sends faxes to Dwight pretending to be Future Dwight warning about poisoned coffee.

evidence.snippet: I took a box of Dwight's stationery, so, from time to time, I send Dwight faxes. From himself. From the future.
"Dwight, at 8 A.M. today, someone poisons the coffee. Do not drink the coffee. More instructions will follow. Cordially, Future Dwight."

beats.summary: Jan informs Michael that the Scranton branch is closing and most employees will be laid off.

evidence.snippet: I am here to tell you that we are closing the Scranton branch.
A small number of people will be transferred to the Stamford branch, and the rest will be getting severance packages.

beats.summary: Michael reacts with disbelief and anger to the branch closing and the decision to lay off most employees.

evidence.snippet: Oh, my god! I don't really get it 'cause we're not doing that bad and our numbers are gonna come up.

beats.summary: Michael announces to the office that the Scranton branch is being shut down.

evidence.snippet: Listen up, everybody… I have some news. We are screwed. Dunder-Mifflin, Scranton is being shut down.

Angela: What about us, Michael? Do we still have jobs?
Michael: I don't know. Probably not.

beats.summary: Dwight and Michael discuss the situation and Dwight offers support.

evidence.snippet: Dwight: When you become close with someone, you develop a kind of sixth sense.
Michael: Well… we have nothin to talk about, Dwight. Just do your work … while you still can.

beats.summary: Various employees react to the news of the branch closing with mixed emotions.

evidence.snippet: Stanley: I couldn't be happier. I'm gonna take the severance and retire.
Pam: It's a blessing in disguise.
